definitions.explanation: A person of outstanding ability in a particular skill or art—especially performing arts, sports, board games, or crafts. Conveys real admiration; not used casually.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はピアノの{名手|めいしゅ}だ。
examples.english: He is a master of the piano.

examples.japanese: {将棋|しょうぎ}の{名手|めいしゅ}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: He is known as a master of shogi.

examples.japanese: {守備|しゅび}の{名手|めいしゅ}と{呼|よ}ばれる{選手|せんしゅ}が{多|おお}いチームは{強|つよ}い。
examples.english: Teams with many players called defensive masters are strong.

notes:
Compound of {名|めい} (renowned, distinguished) + {手|しゅ} (hand, here meaning a person with a skilled hand). Often paired with the domain of skill: ピアノの{名手|めいしゅ}, {弓|ゆみ}の{名手|めいしゅ}, etc.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {名手|めいしゅ}{揃|ぞろ}い: full of masters
- {名手|めいしゅ}{中|ちゅう}の{名手|めいしゅ}: master among masters
- {弓|ゆみ}の{名手|めいしゅ}: master archer
- {守備|しゅび}の{名手|めいしゅ}: defensive virtuoso (sports)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {達人|たつじん}: master; expert — broader, includes everyday domains; less performance-oriented
- {名人|めいじん}: master; champion — often used for board game titles ({将棋|しょうぎ} {名人|めいじん})
- {上手|じょうず}な{人|ひと}: skilled person — everyday and much weaker praise
